title: Start with something the learner can already judge
before: The learner has everyday experience but no technical vocabulary.
after: They can state the question in their own words.
sequence: Identify the missing explanation before introducing its name.

source.title: Grant Sanderson — advice for making explanations
source.locator: FAQ: advice for making math videos

observation: Sanderson recommends examples before general frameworks and putting the key exercise near the opening.
interpretation: Begin with a judgment the learner can make before asking them to adopt new terminology.
example: In the derivative lesson, a moving car gives a familiar starting point for discussing speed.
avoid: Assuming everyday experience supplies technical understanding.
Using a story that adds more unfamiliar things than it explains.
check: Can a beginner describe the problem without using the new term?
